history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 1521 / Chandi Mandir (Chandi Devi Temple) - the same real shrine. The Chandi Mandir stands on the Chandigarh-Kalka highway (NH-5) inside the Chandimandir Cantonment (home of the Indian Army's Western Command), about 15 km from Chandigarh. The planned city of Chandigarh ('Chandi's fort') and the cantonment both take their names from this Shakta shrine, which is counted as a Siddh Peeth. Managed by the Shri Mata Mansa Devi Shrine Board, the temple is built in Nagara style and holds shrines to Chandi, Radha Krishna, Hanuman, Shiva and Ram. During Navratri/Durga Puja thousands of devotees visit. CSV state 'Punjab' is WRONG - the temple is in Haryana; CSV town 'Chandigarh' is also wrong (the temple is ~15 km away, in Panchkula district).

name: Chandi Mandir
town_description: Chandimandir is a cantonment town in Panchkula district, Haryana, on the Chandigarh-Kalka highway, headquarters of the Indian Army's Western Command. Both the cantonment and the planned city of Chandigarh ('fort of Chandi') take their names from the Chandi Mandir shrine. It sits against the backdrop of the Shivalik hills, about 15 km from Chandigarh.

travel.railway: Chandigarh Junction (~15 km - verify), on the Kalka-Delhi line; Kalka station is closer (~12 km - verify).
travel.road: On NH-5 (Chandigarh-Kalka highway), about 15 km from Chandigarh; about 10 km from the Mansa Devi Shrine. Reached by taxi/bus from Chandigarh or Panchkula.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Navratri for the festival crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as open daily 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM (verify). Free entry.
